From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production realtime feed intermittent timeouts (BrightLeaf)

Hi all — I pulled the initial traces from the edge and looked at the connection logs. Quick findings:
- We see repeated FIN/RESET sequences originating from a proxy tier in front of the streaming gateway; the gateway logs show a spike in chunked-transfer resets correlated with a backend queue pressure event between 07:20–07:47 PST.
- Error pattern: clients get 1–3 token chunks (partial payload), then connection close. Retries sometimes reattach successfully.
- Initial metrics: 11.8% request error increase for streaming endpoints in BL's tenant, p99 latency for initial tokens increased from ~230ms -> ~720ms during the spike window.

Actions taken:
1) Scoped the customer traffic and increased connection buffer at the edge to reduce early connection resets.
2) Throttled a noisy downstream job that appeared to cause queue pressure.

Request for BrightLeaf: can we get a full packet capture or a client-side timeline (Wireshark-style) and any proxy configs? That will let us validate whether resets are network-level or application-level.

I attached a small trace dump and our preliminary diagnostics (capture-logs-20261125.tar.gz).

-Hannah
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production realtime feed intermittent timeouts (BrightLeaf) — root cause and rollout plan

Team — quick technical summary for the exec note:
Hypothesis: a bursty downstream worker caused a transient backlog in our streaming dispatcher, which triggered buffer exhaustion at the proxy layer and produced premature connection resets (partial chunk transmission followed by close). Confidence: medium-high (correlated traces + queue depth metrics).

Proposed immediate plan (non-invasive):
1) Keep the increased edge buffer in place (safe for 72 hours) — reduces early TCP/TLS resets and should cut client-visible partial-chunk closes by ~70% based on local repro.
2) Deploy a conservative rate limiter in the dispatcher to smooth backend fan-out (can be rolled in 30m with canary).
3) Post-rollout: enable additional observability flags and a short-lived sampling of full payload traces for BrightLeaf tenant.

Risks: rate limiter may add modest tail latency for high-throughput bursts (we'll canary at 10% traffic and monitor p95/p99).

If agreed, Hannah will push the rate-limiter canary tonight and I'll prepare the rollback script. Also attaching a timeline screenshot summarizing the spike (conn-timeline-11-29.png).

-Dev Patel
Principal Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
